ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all limited partners, the general partner, and every ultimate beneficial owner against (i) FINTRAC's published Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, (ii) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions and terrorist financing designations, (iii) OFAC SDN and sectoral lists given the USD payment rails, and (iv) domestic PEP indicators per FINTRAC's PEP policy guidance; continuous monitoring during the relationship with re-screening on material ownership changes; all findings must be memorialized in a written AML/KYC onboarding record retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation module for Limited Partnerships, available via https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry and licensed corporate registry service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement under the Alberta Partnership Act and applicable name regulations that a limited partnership name must be in English or French (Latin script), legible, and not confusingly similar to any existing Alberta, federal, or extra-provincial registered name; the name must contain a mandatory legal element such as 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'société en commandite', or 's.e.c.'; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script for the registry; a distinguishing element must be added when a NUANS search reports a confusing similarity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name rejection notice from the Alberta Registrar of Companies, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration with the Registrar annexing a fresh NUANS search report, the original rejection notice, and a proposed distinguishing element; if the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may commence judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of the final administrative decision; where rejection was based on a prohibited or regulated token, prior written approval from the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., OSFI for banking/insurance terms) must be obtained and the name resubmitted before the expiry of the NUANS reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or corporate service provider location is permissible as the Alberta registered office and address for service, provided the address is a physical location within Alberta (no PO Box only) capable of accepting and forwarding service of process; however, for Canada-US Tax Treaty substance planning and CRA commercial substance expectations, the limited partnership should maintain substantive outsourced administrative functions or physical presence in Alberta commensurate with its activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated below 5% per annum of unannounced on-site physical inspections for a low-risk, non-regulated PropTech SaaS limited partnership; the inspection risk rises to a moderate probability if FINTRAC/OSFI assessments, CRA regional tax audits, or Service Alberta registered-office verification reviews are commenced.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 51-78; registration and fee rules administered under the Partnership Regulations; the Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 does not apply to a Limited Partnership, which is a pass-through entity taxed under Income Tax Act (Canada) s. 96
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Partnerships Division, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (statutory form also referred to as Registration of Limited Partnership on the Corporate Registry form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement and no escrow-account rule applies to an Alberta Limited Partnership. The Declaration must state each limited partner's contribution, and the contribution must be in money or other property having value, not services (Partnership Act s. 55). Contributions may be funded in cash on subscription or by agreed installments under the partnership agreement; no paid-up capital filing is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [LP NAME], Alberta Limited Partnership: RESOLVED: (1) the capital subscriptions of the General Partner and limited partners, as set out in the Declaration, are approved; (2) the registered office is established at 4000, 333-11th Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta T2R 1L9, Canada, and partnership records maintained there; (3) [Name] is appointed Managing Partner and [Name] Authorized Signatory, empowered to execute banking, contract, and filing documents; (4) such officers are directed to file the Declaration with the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain all required business and data-privacy authorizations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Name Search and Name Reservation (NUANS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online name search portal and authorized registry service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed Limited Partnership names through the Corporate Registry's NUANS pre-screen or name reservation service to verify that the proposed name is distinct from existing Alberta and federal names and satisfies the Partnership Act business-name rules. Consider using a numbered LP name (e.g., 1234567 Alberta Limited Partnership) if brand clearance is pending. The Name Search Report remains valid for 90 days and must be attached to the Declaration.
required_dossiers: List of proposed names (up to three)
Proof of applicant authority for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or non-compliance, file the next alternate name and refile the report, or obtain a written consent / letter of non-objection from the conflicting nameholder and resubmit; a refused name does not affect the underlying registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner(s) and initial limited partners (private execution); subsequently accepted by the Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutory Declaration of Limited Partnership on the Corporate Registry form stating the LP name, registered office in Alberta, mailing address, general partner name and address, aggregate capital contribution of each limited partner, and the latest date on which the limited partnership must expire if fixed term. Execute the Declaration by the general partner and each subscriber; where a corporate general partner is used, attach a certified board resolution or incumbency certificate showing signatory authority.
required_dossiers: Corporate authorization / incumbency certificate for corporate general partner
Proposed registered office address and landlord consent form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any omissions in the contribution schedules or signatory blocks before submission; if an execution defect is detected after filing, resubmit an amended Declaration under the registry's change/correction procedure rather than making a new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Verification of the Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta notary public, lawyer, or commissioner for oaths authorized to verify declarations under the Partnership Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure each subscription and signature is verified before a notary or commissioner of oaths. For signatories outside Canada, obtain notarial certification and, where applicable, an apostille or consular legalization for use in Alberta. The notarized Declaration and attached statutory declaration must attest that the particulars are true and may be relied on by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Statutory declaration of the general partner
Certified true copies of identity / corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the verification, re-execute before an Alberta-recognized notary and attach a fresh statutory declaration; foreign execution may require re-legalization through the consular chain before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration and Statutory Registration with Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) filing window, online Corporate Registration portal, or authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration, valid Name Search Report, and the applicable government fee (CAD 135 / approx. USD 100) through the Corporate Registry online system or an authorized agent. The Registrar reviews for completeness, stamps the Declaration, and records the Limited Partnership in the Partnerships Register. The registration number and effective date are assigned upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, respond within 30 days with corrected documentation or an amended page; failure to cure results in abandonment, requiring a new filing and fee. An adverse decision may be appealed to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate Registration, Registered Office Adoption, and Initial Governance Effect
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) for issuance; General Partner for governance activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, receive the Certificate of Limited Partnership or official registration extract showing the registration number and date. The General Partner then activates the First Board Resolution: confirms the registered office in Alberta, appoints the Managing Partner and Authorized Signatory, and executes the formal Limited Partnership Agreement and banking account mandate. File any notice of change of registered office if the office moves after filing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership / official registration extract
Executed First Resolution of the General Partner
Bank account mandate and KYC / beneficial ownership package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error, request a correction through the registry's change/correction forms; if governance documents conflict with the filed Declaration, amend the Declaration and registry record before relying on the governance terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations, Compliance Program, and Municipal Business Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); municipal business licensing office (City of Calgary / Edmonton); Alberta Workers' Compensation Board and privacy authorities only as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Limited Partnership with CRA for a Business Number (BN), elect GST/HST registration (mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), and open a CRA payroll account if employees are hired. The partnership files an annual T5013 information return; each general and limited partner reports their flow-through share under Income Tax Act s. 96. Obtain the municipal General Business Licence. For the rental-screening module, implement PIPEDA consent and accuracy obligations; if consumer credit reports are supplied, register and comply with Alberta's Fair Trading Act consumer-reporting regime.
required_dossiers: Partner tax identifiers or Form NR/T3 summary for non-residents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, resubmit with the Certificate and an explanatory letter; for late account registration or penalties, invoke CRA's Voluntary Disclosures Program or relief under Income Tax Act s. 220(3.1); if municipal licensing rejects the application because no industrial premises exist, apply for the home / office-based business licence class.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None - no industrial licensing board applies to a cloud-based PropTech SaaS. The relevant authority is the municipal business licensing office (e.g., City of Calgary or Edmonton Business Licensing); where the platform supplies tenant-screening credit reports, the Alberta Fair Trading Act consumer-reporting oversight regime applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operating or manufacturing permit is required for digital services. Voluntary or conditional registrations: Municipal General Business Licence; Consumer Reporting Agency authorization under the Fair Trading Act if the SaaS undertakes tenant-screening credit reporting.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Environmental Assessment Division; federal liaison with Environment and Climate Change Canada for greenhouse gas reporting only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative / office and cloud-SaaS operations; no statutory EIA registration or environmental approval required for intangible digital services with no land disturbance or industrial discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, VOC, or process emissions from software operations. Applicable standards: e-waste / electronics diversion to AEPA-accepted recyclers; office energy and waste management under municipal bylaws; mandatory federal GHG reporting applies only if the LP directly owns data-centre hardware above the 10 kt CO2e/year reporting threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy and fire safety clearance under the Alberta Fire Code and adopted National Fire Code is required for any leased office, including fire marshal inspection, alarm and extinguisher certification, and an approved fire-safety plan. Occupational clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 and OHS Code 2009 (AR 87/2009) requires workplace hazard assessment, worker orientation, and ergonomic compliance for computer workstations. No special structural-load permit is required for standard office / IT tenant improvements; a municipal building permit must be obtained before occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - canada.ca/taxes, including the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal. Alberta does not administer a provincial sales tax; Alberta corporate income tax is administered separately by the Alberta Treasury Board and Finance (Tax and Revenue Administration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or domestic limited partnership must first obtain a CRA Business Number (BN). Procedure: (1) submit Form RC1 'Request for GST/HST Registration' or apply online through CRA Business Registration Online; (2) provide the partnership's legal name, governing jurisdiction, principal address, and a Canadian contact/agent if non-resident; (3) CRA issues a 9-digit BN with a program account code (e.g., 'RT' for GST/HST); (4) the LP must make all subsequent filings electronically via CRA My Business Account; (5) registration is mandatory if taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 over the preceding four calendar quarters, or if the LP is a non-resident engaged in Canadian commercial activity above that threshold; registration below the threshold is voluntary, subject to limited exceptions for non-resident real property vendors.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: an Alberta limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes, with each partner reporting their respective share of income, losses, and capital attributes; for GST/HST purposes, however, the LP is a separate 'person' required to register, collect, and remit tax on its taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a U.S.-style 'check-the-box' entity classification election. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) Income Tax Act section 216 election for non-resident partners to be assessed on net Canadian rental income instead of gross Part XIII withholding; (ii) Excise Tax Act section 156 election for closely related corporations/partnerships to treat certain supplies as made for nil consideration for GST/HST; (iii) joint venture elections under the Excise Tax Act to designate one participant as GST/HST filer; and (iv) hybrid mismatch arrangement rules under amended Canadian tax law, which apply automatically and do not permit elective neutrality for cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - Canadian value-added tax system (5% federal GST; Alberta has no provincial sales tax, resulting in a combined rate of 5% on taxable supplies in Alberta)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (the small supplier threshold); registration is mandatory upon crossing that amount, and non-resident suppliers of Canadian real property should confirm whether a lower or immediate registration obligation applies under the Excise Tax Act and CRA administrative policy.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, pre-clearance stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate. A GST/HST invoice must include prescribed particulars: supplier name and GST/HST registration number, invoice date, description of supply, total amount, tax payable, and any zero-rated or exempt designation. Electronic invoices and e-records are accepted provided they are legible and retained; CRA may require electronic access to records. No government-operated API clearance or digital stamping applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of cloud/SaaS services to a non-resident (not registered for GST/HST) is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, section 7 of the Excise Tax Act if the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada and is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada. For a PropTech platform providing property management and rental screening software, zero-rating may apply where the customer is outside Canada, the subscription is paid from outside Canada, and the software is accessed and used primarily outside Canada. Zero-rating is denied if the service relates to Canadian real property, Canadian residents, or Canadian property management operations; in such cases GST/HST at 5% must be charged. The supplier must maintain documentary evidence of non-resident status and place of use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) for any physical hardware or tangible deliverables, where applicable
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for any exported tangible goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/ACH/SWIFT evidence showing payment from a non-resident bank account
Executed SaaS subscription agreement or cloud service order stating the non-resident customer's jurisdiction
Customer tax identification number, business registration certificate, or passport/official ID demonstrating non-resident status
Technical usage logs, IP geolocation reports, or customer location attestation showing the place of use is outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated export claims within the normal four-year reassessment period, with no time limit where misrepresentation, neglect, carelessness, or wilful default is established. On audit failure, CRA retroactively disallows zero-rating, recovers any claimed input tax credits/refunds, and charges daily compound interest on the resulting 5% GST/HST liability. The Excise Tax Act imposes penalties for false statements or omissions of the greater of CAD 250 and up to 25% of the net tax amount, with gross negligence penalties potentially reaching higher amounts; criminal prosecution is possible for fraudulent export zero-rating claims, and partners of an LP may face civil liability to the extent of the partnership's compliance obligations and applicable indemnity provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Act. Capital account transactions are subject to review and potential restrictions by the Minister of Finance for national economic policy reasons. Profit remittances to non-resident partners are generally permitted with supporting documentation including beneficial ownership certificates and tax filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must surrender all export proceeds to a Canadian bank within 90 days of receipt under the Export and Import Permits Act. No mandatory conversion ratio applies; proceeds must be converted to Canadian dollars unless specific exemptions are granted by the Bank of Canada.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for licensed platforms such as Stripe and PayPal subject to FINTRAC registration and full AML/KYC compliance; offshore digital EMIs face legal constraints including provincial money services business licensing and restrictions on cross-border transfers without proper authorization.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for standard corporate and partnership accounts with electronic KYC verification; physical appearance of directors or authorized signatories is required only for complex structures, high-value transactions exceeding CAD 50,000, or when requested by the bank for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or involvement of high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters, beneficial ownership certificates, source of wealth documentation, and corporate resolution authorizing the account

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols utilize SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'EQTY' for equity injections. Verification requires corporate resolution, ownership proof, tax identification numbers, and beneficial ownership declarations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include SWIFT MT103 for direct payments and issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit under ICC UCP 600 rules for international trade transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return including Alberta Schedule 50 (Provincial/Territorial Partner Information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta Finance receives the provincial schedule through the T5013 data exchange
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus five months if any partner is a corporation or non-resident; fiscal year-end plus 90 days if all partners are Canadian-resident individuals. Calendar-year partnerships: March 31 for individual-only partnerships; May 31 for partnerships with corporate or non-resident partners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 10 per day, capped at CAD 1,000, under Income Tax Act subsections 162(2) through 162(6); additional gross-negligence penalties and CRA enforcement may apply; administrative strike-off of the Alberta LP does not apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (Business Number remittance) for the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before three months after the end of the LP's GST/HST fiscal year; December 31 fiscal year-end is due March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty under the Excise Tax Act: 5% of unremitted net tax plus 1% per complete month late, up to 10%, with prescribed interest compounding daily; the LP remains liable for assessed net tax and interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: NR4 Statement of Amounts Paid or Credited to Non-Residents of Canada and NR4 Summary, if non-resident limited partners receive distributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Non-Resident Withholding Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: February 28 after the calendar year for paper filing; March 31 after the calendar year when filed electronically through CRA-approved services.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late information-return penalties apply; failure to withhold and remit 25% Part XIII tax on non-resident partner distributions makes the LP liable for unremitted tax, interest, and penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the Alberta Partnership Act for a private limited partnership. A statutory audit is required only if the LP is a reporting issuer under Alberta securities law or if CRA or an applicable regulator imposes an audit; otherwise, the LP agreement or an investor or senior lender covenant supplies any audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is acceptable; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is required if the LP is publicly accountable or if investor agreements mandate IFRS. SaaS subscription revenue is recognized under IFRS 15 or ASPE Section 3400, with supplemental US GAAP ASC 606 reporting where investor-level reporting requires it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate public UBO annual registry filing for limited partnerships. The general partner must, at least annually, confirm its own individuals-with-significant-control register when the general partner is an Alberta or federal corporation, recording changes within 15 days. For the LP, the general partner should issue a signed annual ownership confirmation, update the partner register for transfers or admissions, and file an Alberta declaration of amendment only for registry-record changes such as general partner identity, registered office, or registered business scope.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of general and limited partners with names, addresses, capital contributions, and distributions
Minute book containing annual resolutions, general-partner consents, transfer approvals, and authority records
Capital contribution and profit/loss allocation register reflecting each limited partner's entitlement and any transfer of partnership interests
Individuals with significant control register maintained by the corporate general partner, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-750 per annum when a commercial registered agent in Alberta is engaged; near zero if the LP uses the general partner's Alberta office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000-45,000 for a full certified audit if contractually required; USD 8,000-18,000 for an agreed-upon review engagement for a SaaS LP with no statutory audit
